name: FastCDC and gear-hash content-defined chunking. Aliases: CDC, content-defined chunking, variable-size chunking, Gear hash / gearhash, FastCDC-2016 (USENIX ATC'16) and FastCDC-2020 (IEEE TPDS, the 'rolling two bytes' revision). Ancestors and siblings in the same family: Rabin fingerprinting (Rabin 1981; LBFS, SOSP 2001), Buzhash (cyclic polynomial), AE (Asymmetric Extremum), RAM (Rapid Asymmetric Maximum), MII, PCI, BFBC, local-maximum chunking (Bjorner/Blass/Gurevich). Reference implementations: fastcdc-rs, rust-gearhash, fastcdc-py, restic (Rabin), borg and casync (Buzhash), Hugging Face Xet (gearhash, 64 KiB target).
kind: Research result plus a family of algorithms with widely deployed open-source implementations. Not a standard, not a browser feature, not a service. The Hugging Face Xet chunking document is the closest thing to a written specification, and notably it specifies gearhash CDC with min/max clamps rather than FastCDC proper.
maturity: Production and stable. Rabin-CDC has been in production since LBFS (2001) and Venti (2002). Gear hash was introduced in Ddelta (2014); FastCDC published at USENIX ATC 2016 and extended in IEEE TPDS 2020. Shipping in restic, borg, casync, Duplicacy, Kopia, Tarsnap, Bupstash, and Hugging Face Xet. Active research continues on SIMD acceleration (SS-CDC 2019; vector-instruction chunking, arXiv:2508.05797, 2025) and, since 2025, on the security of the construction rather than its speed.
license: The algorithms themselves are unencumbered published academic work. Implementations are permissive: fastcdc-rs is MIT, rust-gearhash is MIT/Apache-2.0 dual, fastcdc-py is MIT, and the cdc-algorithm-tester harness from the independent Delft/Darmstadt study is open source. Permits use in this project without restriction. [uncertain] on whether any Dell/EMC or Microsoft deduplication patent (several surfaced while searching, e.g. US8918375 on chunk-size distribution, US8639669 on optimal chunk sizes) reads on a specific parameterisation; the base gear-hash construction predates and sits outside them, but no clearance opinion was obtained here.
keeps_and_discards: CDC keeps every byte of its input: it is a segmentation, not an extraction, and is lossless by construction. What it discards is not content but IDENTITY. After chunking, a byte range is addressed by the hash of the chunk containing it, so anything smaller than a chunk has no name. For this project that inverts the usual question. With the Hugging Face Xet parameters (8 KiB minimum, 64 KiB target, 128 KiB maximum) a chunk is roughly 2k-16k tokens of prose, larger than most whole pages, so CDC would emit exactly one chunk for essentially every node in a DOM trie and would discard nothing while also achieving nothing. With FastCDC research defaults (2 KiB minimum, 8 KiB target) the same holds for the median DOM text node, which is tens of bytes. The interesting number is therefore not what CDC drops but the fraction of nodes large enough for it to have any effect. The degenerate case is written into the specification itself: if the input is shorter than MIN_CHUNK_SIZE the whole input is emitted as one chunk, which is bit-for-bit the node content hash the project already stores. CDC only earns anything on fat nodes - a long article body serialised as one markdown blob, a <pre> code block, a large table flattened to markdown, an inlined JSON-LD script. Discarding nothing while adding one index row per 8-64 KiB is the honest summary.
structure_preserved: None. CDC operates on a flat byte stream and is indifferent to nesting, order beyond sequence, tabular relations and shadow boundaries. That is a genuine strength against structure_agnosticism - there is no page-structure heuristic anywhere in the algorithm - and simultaneously the reason it cannot be the primary index. A chunk boundary can and routinely does fall in the middle of a table cell, across a shadow-root boundary if a composed serialisation is chunked as one stream, or between an element's opening tag and its text. The composition choice is therefore load-bearing: chunking the WHOLE composed serialisation as one stream produces boundaries that are functions of unrelated siblings and destroys the address/content separation the trie depends on; chunking PER TERMINAL NODE keeps the trie's structural key authoritative and confines CDC to the leaf payload. The independent Delft/Darmstadt study makes the analogous point at file granularity: they had to concatenate their datasets into one stream to compare algorithms, and note explicitly that this can prevent even identical files from being detected as duplicates because chunks form across file boundaries.
interactive_elements: Not handled and not addressable. CDC has no notion of a control, a role, or an event handler. If a serialised button's text lands inside a chunk it is preserved as bytes; the chunk hash says nothing about whether it is a button. Any interactivity marking must come from the layer above - the trie key and the tag-plus-interactivity annotation - and CDC must be applied strictly downstream of it, to the node's text payload, never to a serialisation interleaving control markup with prose. Applying CDC above the tag layer would make an interactivity flag change look like a content change and vice versa.
interactive_state_fidelity: Zero on its own, and this is the axis where a naive 'hash the serialised page' design silently fails. Disabled, checked, selected, expanded and aria-* states are properties of the element, not of a byte range; whether they survive depends entirely on whether the serialiser feeding CDC emitted them. If it did not, a checkbox toggling from unchecked to checked produces an identical chunk hash and the change is invisible to the delta pipeline - a false negative, not a cost. If it did, every state flip rewrites the chunk containing it, and because state changes are frequent and small while chunks are large (8-64 KiB), one aria-expanded flip invalidates a whole chunk. The token cost of carrying state is thus paid twice under CDC: once in the representation and again in delta amplification. The design conclusion for this project is that interactive state belongs in the trie key or in a separately hashed per-node attribute vector, NOT inside the CDC-chunked text payload, so a state flip is a cheap key-level delta rather than a chunk rewrite.
layout_awareness: None at any stage. CDC never reads geometry, computed style, bounding boxes or paint, and there is no point in the algorithm where layout could enter even accidentally. It is the cleanest item in this research set against no_layout_in_the_fold. The corollary is the mirror-image weakness: CDC cannot detect CSS-driven visual change either, because a change altering only rendering and not the byte stream produces an identical chunk sequence.
javascript_required: No. CDC runs over whatever byte stream it is given, in the browser or in Python, with no dependence on page scripts. In this project the chunker would sit on the Python side consuming already-serialised node text; it fires no page code, touches no DOM API, and cannot trigger telemetry. The JavaScript question is entirely about the layer that produced the text, not about the chunker.
evaluation_method: The field's protocol is: assemble a corpus of versioned or naturally redundant files, concatenate into a stream, run each chunker, hash chunks with a cryptographic digest, and report four metrics - throughput (MiB/s), deduplication ratio, mean chunk size, chunk-size standard deviation. Unusually for this research set there is now a rigorous INDEPENDENT execution of it: Gregoriadis, Balduf, Scheuermann and Pouwelse (TU Delft / TU Darmstadt), 'A Thorough Investigation of Content-Defined Chunking Algorithms for Data Deduplication', arXiv:2409.06066v3, submitted to IEEE Transactions on Cloud Computing. They reimplemented Rabin, Buzhash, Gear, Gear64, SIMD Gear64, AE, RAM, MII, PCI, BFBC and FastCDC's Normalized Chunking in one Rust harness, ran each 10 times per dataset/algorithm/target with a warm-up on an idle machine, and published harness plus dataset-construction scripts. The critical methodological gap for this project: nobody evaluates CDC on the workload that matters here - many small independent strings addressed by structural key - because the entire literature assumes large files or a concatenated stream.
corpus_size_and_origins: The independent study used four real datasets plus one synthetic, each approximately 10 GiB, with entropy measured as post-GZIP size ratio: RAND (100.0%, generated random binary), LNX (98.6%, Linux ISO images across distributions and versions), PDF (87.5%, over 2000 arXiv research papers), WEB (72.8%, daily snapshots of nytimes.com for all of 2022 pulled from the Internet Archive and crawled three levels deep - explicitly a mix of HTML/CSS/JS with images, video and fonts, of which BINARY IS 89% OF THE CONTENT BY VOLUME), and CODE (22.1%, 94 versions of GCC, GDB and Emacs source distributions). The WEB dataset is the only web-derived corpus found anywhere in the CDC literature: it is ONE origin (nytimes.com plus three link levels), from ONE year (2022), 89% non-text, one English news publisher. Any number quoted from it for this project must carry that reach - the text portion that actually resembles a DOM fold is roughly a ninth of it. FastCDC's own 2016 and 2020 evaluations used backup, VM-image and source-code datasets, not web content. There is no CDC evaluation on a corpus of DOM subtrees, none on multilingual web text, and none at the sub-kilobyte string sizes this project's nodes actually occupy.
reported_precision_recall: Precision and recall are not this field's metrics and CDC is lossless, so a fidelity precision/recall does not apply; deduplication ratio and throughput stand in. From the INDEPENDENT harness (Intel Xeon Gold 6154 @ 3.00 GHz, target 2 KiB, RAND dataset, median of 10 runs, MiB/s): fixed-size chunking 2529; SIMD Gear64 941; RAM 887; BFBC-on-CODE 876; AE 734; BFBC 620; Gear32 599; BFBC* 596; Gear64 470; Buzhash 338; PCI 308; MII 256; Rabin 202. FastCDC's own headline claim is 'about 10x faster than the best open-source Rabin-based CDC and about 3x faster than state-of-the-art Gear- and AE-based CDC', and '3-10x faster while achieving nearly the same and even higher deduplication ratio'. The independent numbers put scalar Gear at 599/202 = 2.96x over Rabin and SIMD Gear at 4.7x, so the 10x figure is NOT reproduced by an impartial reimplementation on a modern CPU - it is recoverable only against a slow Rabin baseline. On deduplication ratio the independent finding is that the classic sliding-window algorithms (Rabin, Buzhash, Gear) are still unbeaten, with AE and MII comparable, and that FastCDC's Normalized Chunking at NC-1 to NC-3 costs essentially nothing while substantially reducing chunk-size variance - the largest divergence observed was NC-2 BEATING vanilla Gear by two percentage points at 8 KiB target on CODE. Absolute deduplication ratios are dataset-dominated: roughly 0.6-0.8 on CODE, far lower on LNX (chart axis to ~0.20), lowest on PDF (axis to ~0.06), intermediate on WEB. [uncertain] on the exact WEB deduplication ratio, which is presented only as a figure with no tabulated value.
independent_oracle: Yes, and unusually strong ones on two separate axes. (1) Correctness: CDC is lossless, so concatenating the emitted chunks and comparing to the input is a complete, assumption-free oracle sharing nothing with the chunker's logic. The Hugging Face Xet specification goes further and publishes a golden vector - a named CSV plus a .chunks file of 64-hex-char hashes and lengths - so an implementation is checkable against a fixed external artifact rather than against itself. (2) Published-claim verification: the Delft/Darmstadt reimplementation is a genuine independent oracle over the literature, and several published claims did not survive it. The AE parameterisation formula, disseminated through FastCDC, Destor and DedupBench, yields chunks 13% under target at 512 B and 39% under target at 8 KiB (they notified the tool authors). RAM's chunk-size-variance claim fails on every realistic dataset and RAM produces pathologically large chunks on low-entropy text. BFBC's reported deduplication advantage over Rabin inverts under impartial settings (their Dataset 1: BFBC 79.8% vs Rabin 68.2%; independent CODE run: Rabin 87.1% vs BFBC 85.0%). For this project the usable move is to adopt the golden-vector discipline: any chunker shipped must reproduce the published Xet chunk lengths byte-for-byte before it is allowed into a measured path.
evidence_independence: Mixed and now cleanly separable. The FastCDC 2016 and 2020 numbers are author-run (Xia, Zou, Jiang, Zhou, Liu, Feng et al.), on author-chosen datasets, through the authors' own Destor integration - the exact pattern the independent study names, writing that many researchers promote their algorithm under conditions that fail to hold up, relying on biased datasets, misleading metrics, or narrowly defined test cases. The 2024 Delft/Darmstadt study is the counterweight: different institutions, no stake in any algorithm, published harness and dataset scripts, and it reports discrepancies rather than only confirmations. The Hugging Face Xet document is vendor documentation but publishes a checkable golden vector, which is stronger evidence than a benchmark table. Net rule for this project: source FastCDC throughput and deduplication claims to the independent study, never to the original paper.
page_archetype_coverage:
Effectively absent, and this is the largest evidence gap for this project's intended use. The single web dataset is one news publisher crawled three levels deep, mixing article, listing and collection archetypes without separating them, and 89% binary by volume so the reported ratio is dominated by images and video rather than by any page archetype. There is no per-archetype breakdown anywhere in the CDC literature - no article vs forum vs product vs collection vs listing vs documentation vs service split, and no separation of the long-prose nodes where CDC could help from the short-label nodes where it provably cannot. Predicting from first principles rather than measurement: CDC's value is monotone in node length, so documentation and article archetypes (long

and 

 payloads) are the only ones where it can pay, while product listings, forums, collections and service UIs are dominated by strings below the minimum chunk size and would get exactly zero benefit at a nonzero index cost. That prediction is untested and should be measured on this project's own corpus before adoption.
script_and_locale_behaviour: Structurally script-invariant, which is a real advantage: the gear hash indexes a 256-entry table by BYTE, so it has no tokeniser, no word boundary and no whitespace assumption, and behaves identically on CJK, RTL and whitespace-free segmentation. Two measurable caveats. First, byte-level chunking on UTF-8 will split multi-byte codepoints across boundaries; harmless for deduplication, but it means a chunk is not independently decodable as text and must not be handed to an embedder or a model without rejoining. Second, effective chunk size in CHARACTERS varies by script - CJK at 3 bytes/character means an 8 KiB chunk holds roughly a third the characters of an ASCII chunk, so any token budget derived from chunk counts is script-dependent even though the boundaries are not. The independent study's entropy finding has a locale-shaped corollary: algorithms selecting divisors from byte-pair frequency (BFBC) are dataset-tuned and would need retuning per script (their top pairs on realistic data were NULL-NULL and '/>' from HTML), whereas gear hash needs none. [uncertain] on whether any published CDC evaluation includes non-Latin text at all; none was found.
leaks_outward: The chunker itself discloses nothing to the page - it runs after capture, over bytes already in hand, and makes no network or DOM call. The leak is entirely on the storage and transport side, and as of 2025 it is a documented and exploited class rather than a theoretical concern. Truong et al., 'Breaking and Fixing Content-Defined Chunking' (ACM CCS 2025; IACR eprint 2025/558), demonstrate efficient key-recovery attacks against five keyed CDC schemes deployed in Borg, Bupstash, Duplicacy, Restic and Tarsnap: publicly observable chunk boundaries convert into algebraic equations over the scheme's prime modulus, multipliers and coefficient maps, reducing the keyspace enough to recover the secret. Separately, arXiv:2504.02095 ('Chunking Attacks on File Backup Services using Content-Defined Chunking') shows protocol-agnostic fingerprinting and partial content extraction from observed chunk-length sequences alone, and the encrypted-deduplication frequency-analysis line (arXiv:1904.05736) maps ciphertext chunks to plaintext by size locality. The direct consequence: a chunk-length sequence is itself a fingerprint of the page content, so if chunk metadata ever escapes - shared index, remote store, telemetry, even on-disk file sizes - page content is partially recoverable without the content. If chunk boundaries never leave the local store, this reduces to nothing.
mechanism_detectability: Zero. CDC patches no browser API, requires no CDP domain, installs no extension, and executes strictly after the page has been read. There is no attachShadow patch, no Runtime.enable, no injected script, and no timing signature visible to the page because the work happens out of process. This is the best possible answer against closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: adopting CDC cannot make the reader any more detectable than it already is, because CDC never touches the reader's side of the boundary. The only detectability it could add is second-order - if chunking cost gated a subsequent page interaction, the delay could in principle be observed - which does not arise in a design where the actuator layer and the fold are separate.
countermeasures: Against the chunk-boundary leakage class the published mitigations are: replace the rolling hash with a cryptographic PRF (an HMAC-keyed gear table) so boundaries are not algebraically invertible; enlarge the keyspace so the CCS 2025 equation-solving attack does not close; randomise or pad chunk lengths to break the length-sequence fingerprint; or simply never expose chunk metadata beyond the local trust boundary. Against the degenerate-chunk failure the countermeasures are the standard clamps - minimum and maximum chunk size, cut-point skipping, and Normalized Chunking - with the independent study confirming that NC costs nothing in deduplication ratio while cutting variance, which makes NC the free countermeasure. For this project's specific risk (a delta guarantee being wrong rather than expensive), the countermeasures are a full-width cryptographic chunk digest rather than a truncated one, storing per-node length alongside the chunk list, and recording chunk COUNT so a same-length substitution is detectable.
measured_fidelity_cost: Measured rather than asserted for the performance hardenings, absent for the security ones. Normalized Chunking: NC-1 through NC-3 against vanilla Gear, across four datasets and seven target sizes, showed only marginal detrimental effect, the largest single divergence being NC-2 EXCEEDING vanilla by two percentage points at 8 KiB target on CODE - i.e. the variance-reduction hardening is free or better, against a vanilla-Gear control. Minimum-chunk-size skipping: raises throughput and is documented by Xet as a pure search optimisation that provably does not change the emitted chunk set (the scan pointer advances by up to MIN_CHUNK_SIZE - 64 - 1, and because gear's window is 64 bytes the first admissible test still sees a fully mixed hash), at the cost of forbidding boundaries in the first MIN_CHUNK_SIZE bytes - which is exactly the mechanism making short nodes single chunks. SIMD acceleration: roughly 2x over scalar Gear64 (941 vs 470 MiB/s) with identical boundaries, so zero fidelity cost; Xet states explicitly that SIMD paths produce the same boundaries as the scalar path. The security hardenings (HMAC gear table, length padding) have NO published fidelity or throughput measurement found here; substituting a PRF for a table lookup would be expected to cost far more than 2x, but that is an estimate, not a measurement. [uncertain] on the measured cost of PRF-based chunking.
gate_state_at_capture: Not applicable to the chunker and not representable in it. CDC has no notion of a consent banner, paywall, login wall or CAPTCHA; it chunks whatever bytes it is handed. This is a real hazard for a corpus built on top of it: a paywalled article stub and the full article produce completely different chunk sets, so a store mixing gated and ungated captures of the same URL shows them as unrelated content rather than as two states of one document, and the deduplication ratio is silently depressed. The remedy lives entirely at the layer above - gate state must be a field of the trie key or the node record, never something the chunk layer is expected to infer. If gate state is in the key, CDC composes correctly: two gate states become two addresses, each with its own chunk list.
determinism: Complete and by design, within a fixed parameter set. Same bytes, same gear table, same mask, same min/max clamps -> bit-identical chunk boundaries on every platform. The Xet specification states the requirements explicitly: fixed 256-entry table and mask, byte-wise updates so endianness is irrelevant, 64-bit wrapping arithmetic on h = (h << 1) + TABLE[b], hash reset only at an emitted boundary so streaming in arbitrary pieces gives the same result as a single pass, and SIMD paths that must agree with scalar. The independent study confirms the practical form: deduplication ratio and chunk-size distribution results are machine-independent because the algorithms are deterministic, and only throughput varies with hardware. This is the strongest determinism story of any item in this research set.
determinism_across_versions: Stable across browser and OS versions - CDC has no browser dependency at all, which removes an entire drift class that the DOM-side and AX-tree-side items in this research suffer from. The drift risk is entirely in the PARAMETERS, and there it is total: changing the gear table, the mask width, the minimum or maximum chunk size, or the normalisation level re-chunks the whole store and invalidates every stored chunk hash. There is no partial migration and no graceful path. FastCDC-2016 and FastCDC-2020 are described as producing the same cut points (the 2020 'rolling two bytes' change being 30-40% faster with identical boundaries), but Gear32 and Gear64 do NOT agree with each other, and an implementation using a different published table does not agree either. Operational rule: the parameter tuple must be versioned in the store alongside every chunk hash, a parameter change must be treated as a full re-index and budgeted as such, and it must never be applied silently.
reproducibility: High and externally checkable, better than anything else in this research set. A result can be re-obtained years later from the bytes alone - no browser, no network, no model - because the algorithm is a pure function. The Hugging Face Xet reference vector makes this concrete: a published input file plus a published list of chunk hashes and lengths any implementation must reproduce exactly. The Delft/Darmstadt study publishes its harness (github.com/mrd0ll4r/cdc-algorithm-tester), its chunking library, its dataset-construction scripts and interactive result charts. The one reproducibility hole is the corpus, and it is real: the WEB dataset is daily nytimes.com snapshots from the Internet Archive, a moving target - Archive availability, robots-driven retroactive exclusions and the site's own evolution mean a re-crawl years later does not yield the same 10 GiB. The chunker is reproducible; the web corpus it was measured on is not.
failure_modes: Five, ordered by how they would actually bite this project. (1) DEGENERATE SHORT INPUT - input shorter than MIN_CHUNK_SIZE emits exactly one chunk. For a DOM node trie this is not an edge case, it is the common case: at 8 KiB minimum (Xet) or 2 KiB (FastCDC research default) the overwhelming majority of DOM text nodes never reach a boundary test, so CDC is a no-op that still costs an index row. (2) PATHOLOGICAL LARGE CHUNKS - a region where the boundary condition is rarely satisfied runs to MAX_CHUNK_SIZE and is cut at a POSITION-defined boundary, reintroducing the boundary-shift problem CDC exists to solve. The independent study shows this is entropy-driven and can be severe: RAM produces pathologically large chunks on low-entropy text (CODE) and fails to find boundaries at all. (3) HEAVY-TAILED SIZE DISTRIBUTION - almost all CDC algorithms peak at a minimum size and decay with a long tail, so mean chunk size badly understates variance; sliding-window algorithms with 32-256 B windows produce many small chunks and compensate with a long tail. NC mitigates it. (4) PARAMETER MISMATCH between store versions - two stores share nothing, silently. (5) SECURITY FAILURE - keyed CDC schemes with observable boundaries are key-recoverable (CCS 2025), and chunk-length sequences fingerprint content.
failure_visibility: Mixed, and the dangerous half is silent - which matters given this project's explicit refusal of silent degradation. LOUD: nothing; CDC never raises. QUIET BUT DETECTABLE with one line of instrumentation: the degenerate single-chunk case is visible as chunks_emitted == 1 with length < MIN_CHUNK_SIZE, and the pathological case as size == MAX_CHUNK_SIZE exactly. A chunk-size histogram makes both immediately obvious and should be a permanent metric, not a debugging aid. SILENT AND DANGEROUS: parameter mismatch between store versions - the store simply stops deduplicating and grows, with no error, which is precisely the shape of the INGEST DEGRADATION symptom this project is chasing. Also silent: a within-node change that happens not to move any boundary is still caught (the chunk hash changes), but a change to content the serialiser never emitted - CSS-driven, canvas, video, closed shadow root - produces an identical chunk sequence and reports no-change. That is a false negative in the delta guarantee, and CDC cannot surface it because the missing content never reached the chunker.
scale_limits: Chunking itself is strictly linear in bytes with constant memory - one 64-bit register and two counters - and is not where scale breaks. Cost stops being linear in the CHUNK INDEX, and this bears directly on this project's measured ingest degradation. Every chunk is a row in a hash->location map; at an 8 KiB average a store holds roughly 131k chunks per GiB, and each ingest performs a random-access probe into a structure that outgrows L2, then L3, then RAM. This is the classic deduplication disk-bottleneck problem the storage literature has treated as its central scaling issue since the Data Domain work: the index probe is a random read whose cost is a step function of where the index currently lives, which means it does NOT appear as time attributed to any single call in a call profiler - it appears as cache and TLB misses smeared across whichever call performs the lookup. That is a strong candidate explanation for the observed 2.6x degradation from page 136 to page 500 on identical repeated pages, with cProfile attributing only ~6% of wall time to reachable calls: a call profiler cannot see memory-hierarchy cost, only call cost. The standard remedies, in order of applicability here: a Bloom filter in front of the index so most negative lookups never touch it (converting a random miss into a bit test); locality-preserving caching; stream-informed layout so related chunks are indexed adjacently; sampled indexing (index one chunk in N, find the rest by locality); and sharding by key prefix. The diagnostic that distinguishes this hypothesis from others is a hardware-counter run (perf: cache-misses, dTLB-load-misses, page-faults) rather than another cProfile - the independent CDC study's own methodology, which pairs throughput with perf counters and finds effects invisible in pseudocode complexity, is the direct precedent.
delta_cost_model: PER-CHANGE COST, with CDC applied per terminal trie node: re-chunking a modified node is O(len(node)), not O(page), plus one hash per emitted chunk plus one index probe per chunk. For an edit inside a large node the number of chunks that actually change is bounded - the Xet documentation states the property precisely: an insertion perturbs the chunk containing it and possibly one neighbour, and the MIN/MAX clamps keep the disruption bounded. So a mid-paragraph insertion in a 100 KiB node costs roughly 2 chunk rewrites out of ~13, not 13. That is exactly the half of the delta problem the trie alone cannot solve. CHANGES THAT FALL OUTSIDE THE MODEL, named so the guarantee is falsifiable: (1) any node shorter than MIN_CHUNK_SIZE - one chunk, so ANY edit rewrites 100% of that node's chunks; for a DOM trie this is most nodes, and it is cost with zero benefit rather than cost overrun. (2) A parameter change (table, mask, min, max, NC level) - O(entire store), and SILENT. (3) A change confined to content the serialiser never emitted - CSS-driven visual change, canvas and video pixels, closed shadow roots, and declarative shadow DOM already flattened or missed in the initial parse - costs ZERO and is NEVER DETECTED. CDC does not widen this hole but it does not close it, and it can create a false sense that content hashing is complete. (4) A subtree deletion - one mutation record, but every descendant's chunk list is invalidated: O(subtree), not O(1). (5) The index probe - NOT constant in store size (see scale_limits); a delta claim ignoring it is already false at large store sizes even when the hashing is honestly O(delta). (6) A change near MAX_CHUNK_SIZE, where the clamp turns a content-defined boundary into a position-defined one and the disruption propagates further than the local-perturbation property promises. (7) Attribute-only and interactive-state changes, when state is not in the chunked stream - zero cost, never detected.
reanchoring_stability: CDC gives CONTENT-relative anchoring, orthogonal to and complementary with the trie's ADDRESS-relative anchoring, and the pairing is the interesting result for this project. A chunk hash survives arbitrary movement of the node in the DOM - the same paragraph reappearing under a different xpath still hashes to the same chunks - so chunk hashes are a re-anchoring signal the single-xpath key completely lacks. Conversely a chunk hash does not survive editing, while an xpath does. The two failure modes are disjoint, which is exactly why they compose: exact xpath match first, chunk-hash match as a recorded fallback carrying a confidence field, is a BOUNDED deterministic scheme - both legs are exact equality tests, no fuzzy string distance anywhere, so it does not contaminate the reproducibility claim. Measured re-anchor rates for CDC in a DOM setting do not exist in the literature. The closest proxy is deduplication ratio on the WEB dataset (daily snapshots of one news site), which measures roughly the same thing - what fraction of yesterday's content is still findable today by content alone - but at file granularity and 89% binary, so it does not transfer. This is a cheap measurement this project can make for itself: chunk every node on capture N and capture N+1, and report the fraction of N+1 nodes whose chunk set intersects a capture-N chunk set under a changed xpath. [uncertain] on any published DOM-level chunk re-anchor rate.
adversarial_exposure: CDC is fully layout-blind, so it preserves invisible-to-human content exactly as faithfully as visible content and can filter NOTHING without reading layout. Text in a display:none container, an off-screen aria-hidden block, white-on-white text, and a zero-height div all chunk identically to the visible article. This is a genuine structural exposure and it is worse than the heuristic extractors this project is measured against - Readability-style extractors drop hidden subtrees as a side effect of their heuristics, and a layout-blind fold does not. The honest statement is that CDC neither adds nor removes exposure: it inherits exactly the exposure of the serialiser feeding it. What CDC DOES add on the safety side is a positive: because chunks are content-addressed, a known-malicious injected payload seen on one page is recognisable by chunk hash on every other page with no semantic analysis - a cheap cross-page injection detector the trie alone does not provide. On the negative side, chunk boundaries are attacker-influenceable: an adversary controlling page content controls where boundaries fall, which is the mechanism behind the 2025 chunking attacks, and in a shared store could be used to force collisions or to probe for the presence of other content by observing whether deduplication occurred.
provenance_carrying: None intrinsically - a chunk is a hash and a length, carrying no url, no xpath, no capture time, no shadow depth and no gate state. All provenance must come from the enclosing record. That is not a defect here because the composition is clean: the trie key url:xpath:markdown:content already supplies every provenance field, and CDC attaches BELOW it, so a chunk inherits full provenance from the node that owns it. The design requirement that follows is directional and easy to get wrong: the chunk index must map chunk_hash -> {set of node addresses}, many-to-many, never chunk_hash -> content alone, so a chunk shared between two pages resolves to BOTH provenances rather than losing one. Getting that backwards - treating a deduplicated chunk as belonging to whichever node stored it first - silently destroys provenance for every subsequent occurrence, which is precisely the failure that would break the per-token origin property current injection defences require.
roundtrip_safety: A fixed point by construction and trivially so: concatenating the emitted chunks reproduces the input byte-for-byte, and re-chunking that concatenation yields identical boundaries. There is no escaping policy because there is no encoding - CDC does not transform bytes, it only cuts between them - so there is no injection surface in the chunker itself and no ambiguity to resolve on parse. This makes chunk-list round-tripping the cleanest oracle-free fidelity metric available to this project: if serialise -> chunk -> concatenate -> compare fails, the bug is provably in the serialiser, not the chunker. One caveat, textual rather than binary: a boundary may fall inside a UTF-8 codepoint or inside a markdown construct, so an individual chunk is not independently parseable as text or markdown and must never be displayed, embedded or handed to a model as a standalone unit without rejoining.
token_budget_and_ordering: CDC supplies no ordering or truncation policy of its own - it sits upstream of the token contract entirely. What it does supply is a content-stable unit of truncation: if a node exceeds the budget, dropping whole chunks from the tail is stable across captures in a way a character count is not, because the surviving prefix chunks keep the same hashes and therefore the same identity between visits. That is a genuine, cheap property for a text(budget=...) implementation - truncate on chunk boundaries, report the dropped chunk hashes, and the omission becomes addressable rather than silent, which is the prerequisite for an honest budget contract. Against the recency-dominant position-bias finding this project is tracking, CDC is neutral: it neither helps nor hurts ordering. Note the size mismatch: at 8-64 KiB one chunk is 2k-16k tokens, far coarser than a useful budget granularity, so chunk-boundary truncation requires dropping the target size to roughly 512-1024 bytes, which raises chunk count and index size proportionally - and the index is the resource already under pressure.
representation_cost: Zero tokens added and zero tokens saved: CDC is a segmentation, so the text handed to a model is unchanged, and nothing is lost per token saved because nothing is saved per token. The cost is in STORAGE and INDEX. Per chunk: one cryptographic digest (32 bytes at 256 bits) plus a length plus an index entry, so at an 8 KiB target the metadata overhead is roughly 0.5-1% of content size; at a 512-byte target - the size that would actually be useful for DOM nodes - it rises to roughly 8-15% before index structure overhead. The honest framing is that CDC buys delta locality and cross-page content identity, and pays for them in index rows, which is exactly the resource this project has already measured itself running short of.
what_could_be_adopted: Three specific mechanisms, in descending order of value. (1) PER-NODE CDC ABOVE A SIZE THRESHOLD, as the answer to the within-text half of the delta problem. Apply gearhash CDC only to terminal nodes whose serialised text exceeds a threshold; store that node's content identity as a Merkle root over its chunk hashes; below the threshold keep the plain content hash unchanged. This makes a mid-paragraph insertion cost O(2 chunks) instead of O(node) on the fat nodes where it matters, while costing literally nothing on the short nodes that are the majority. Set the threshold from this project's own node-length distribution, and set the target chunk size far below the storage-literature default - 512 B to 2 KiB, not 64 KiB - because DOM nodes are small. (2) THE GOLDEN-VECTOR DISCIPLINE from the Xet specification: ship a fixed input file and its expected chunk hash/length list as a test, and refuse to run a measured path against a chunker that does not reproduce it. A no-mocks-compatible external oracle that costs nothing. (3) CHUNK HASH AS A SECOND RE-ANCHOR LEG, exact-match only, recorded with a confidence field distinguishing 'xpath matched' from 'xpath moved, content matched' from 'neither'. Explicitly NOT to be adopted: whole-page chunking (destroys the address/content separation), CDC as a substitute for the trie (no structure at all), any keyed-CDC scheme whose boundaries could become observable outside the local store, and unthresholded global chunking (adds index rows to the exact structure whose growth is already the suspected cause of ingest degradation). One adjacent finding worth carrying separately: the independent study's perf-counter methodology, not the chunking algorithm, is the technique most likely to explain this project's profiler-invisible ingest degradation.
constraint_violation_ledger: structure_agnosticism -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS. CDC is byte-level and consults no page-structure heuristic whatsoever; arguably the most structure-agnostic mechanism in this research set. One condition: apply it to raw node text, never to an extractor's cleaned output, or the heuristic enters through the input. Severity: none, given that condition. no_layout_in_the_fold -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS. Reads no geometry at any stage and has no point where geometry could enter. Severity: none. o_delta -- ADOPTABLE IN A BOUNDED FORM, with two declared exceptions. Per-node chunking is genuinely O(len(node)) and bounds within-text delta to about 2 chunks, which is the property being sought. But (a) the chunk INDEX probe is not constant in store size and must be declared as an exception rather than assumed away, and (b) on nodes below MIN_CHUNK_SIZE - most DOM nodes - CDC degenerates to the existing content hash and delivers no delta benefit while still adding an index row. Verdict: adopt above a measured size threshold only; adopting it globally would ADD to the ingest-degradation problem it is meant to help with. Severity: medium if adopted unthresholded, low if thresholded. no_mocks -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS. Pure deterministic computation with a published golden vector; no subsystem to stub and no fallback to degrade into. It strengthens the no-mocks posture rather than straining it. Severity: none. closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed -- ADOPTABLE AS-IS. Patches nothing, requires no page instrumentation, is undetectable by the page, and cannot reach into a closed root any more than the serialiser feeding it can. Severity: none. OVERALL VERDICT: adoptable as-is in the fold, restricted to terminal nodes above a size threshold, with a small target chunk size, a Merkle-root node identity, a golden-vector conformance test, and both the index-probe cost and the never-serialised-content hole written down as named exceptions to the O(delta) claim rather than left implicit.
governance_signal_handling: None, and not applicable - CDC operates entirely after fetch, on bytes already retrieved, and has no notion of robots.txt, Content Signals, ai.txt, the AIPREF vocabulary, Web Bot Auth or HTTP 402. All governance enforcement must live in the fetch layer. One second-order interaction is worth recording: because CDC enables content-level deduplication ACROSS urls, a store that chunks aggressively will silently merge content whose source urls carry different governance signals - an ai.txt-restricted page and an unrestricted page sharing a boilerplate block would share chunks. If governance state is ever to be enforceable per stored artifact, the chunk index must therefore be many-to-many on provenance (see provenance_carrying) so every url claiming a chunk stays attached to it, and deletion driven by a governance signal must remove the url->chunk edge and garbage-collect only unreferenced chunks.
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: CDC neither adds nor removes PII - it is lossless, so any personal data in the input is present in the chunks, and the regulated act under EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 is the persistent storage of page content, which is unchanged by how that content is segmented. Two CDC-specific wrinkles do matter for a stored-artifact posture. First, DELETION: deduplication means one chunk may be referenced by many urls, so an erasure request cannot be satisfied by deleting a url's record - the chunk survives until refcount reaches zero, and a naive implementation retains the content indefinitely while believing it deleted. Reference counting with genuine garbage collection is a compliance requirement here, not an optimisation. Second, INFERENCE: the 2025 chunking-attack results establish that chunk-length sequences alone can fingerprint and partially reconstruct content, so a chunk index stripped of content is NOT anonymised data and must not be treated as safe to export or share. [uncertain] on how EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 specifically treat content-addressed stores and whether a chunk hash of personal data is itself personal data under them; the general direction of pseudonymisation guidance suggests it is, but this was not verified against the text.
